name: firewall-cmd
description: The firewalld control tool used by RHEL, Fedora, CentOS, and openSUSE: zone-based firewall management with runtime and permanent rules.

flags.description: Which zones are active and on which interfaces.
Allow a named service (http, ssh, samba...) in the current zone.
Make the change survive reload/reboot (without it, rules are runtime-only).
Apply all permanent rules to the runtime.
Show everything the current zone allows.

examples.explanation: The current zone's complete rule set — the firewalld equivalent of ufw status verbose.
The firewalld idiom: add permanently, then reload. Forgetting --permanent loses the rule on the next reload.
Opens PostgreSQL to everyone — combine with --add-source=10.0.0.0/24 to restrict to a subnet.

about: firewalld groups interfaces into zones (public, internal, trusted) with per-zone rule sets. The runtime/permanent split is its key concept: changes without --permanent vanish on reload; changes with --permanent do not take effect until --reload. Many tutorials forget one half — check with --list-all after every change.
mistakes: Forgetting --permanent (rule lost at reload) or forgetting --reload (rule not active).
distroNotes: RHEL/CentOS/Fedora/openSUSE default. Debian/Ubuntu use ufw or raw nftables.
